title: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, VARIANT TYPE
alt_titles: XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM WITH NORMAL DNA REPAIR RATES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH), the human homolog of yeast RAD30.

checks.claim: The variant type of xeroderma pigmentosum (XPV) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding DNA polymerase eta (POLH).
checks.evidence_quote: These results indicate that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V
checks.explanation: hRAD30 is the earlier name for POLH (DNA polymerase eta), so the draft is only restating the gene name. The abstract itself never uses 'POLH' or 'polymerase eta'.

checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that this polymerase is a human homologue of the yeast Rad30 protein, recently identified as DNA polymerase eta.
checks.explanation: The paper directly states that the polymerase is the human homologue of yeast Rad30.

paragraphs.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XP-V) is an inherited disorder associated with an increased incidence of sunlight-induced skin cancers (Masutani et al., 1999). Patients show the clinical features of xeroderma pigmentosum, which Robbins et al. (1974) described as an inherited disease with sun sensitivity, multiple cutaneous neoplasms, and abnormal DNA repair. Unlike cells from XP groups A to G, XP-V cells carry out normal or nearly normal nucleotide excision repair of UV-induced DNA damage but are defective in replicating UV-damaged DNA (Masutani et al., 1999; Wang et al., 1991). XP-V cells are only slightly more sensitive than normal cells to the cytotoxic effect of UV radiation, but they are significantly more sensitive to its mutagenic effect (Wang et al., 1991).

paragraphs.text: Lehmann et al. (1975) found that cells from the class of xeroderma pigmentosum patients whose excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers was completely normal (XP variants) had an abnormality in DNA synthesis after UV irradiation. These variant cells took much longer than normal cells to convert the low-molecular-weight DNA first made after UV irradiation into high-molecular-weight DNA. Caffeine strongly inhibited this slow conversion in UV-irradiated XP variant cells but had no effect in normal cells. Two excision repair-deficient XP cell lines showed intermediate effects, both in the time needed for the conversion and in the degree to which caffeine inhibited it.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) studied 2 independent Japanese families with 2 photosensitive patients identified as having XPV. Cells from the heterozygous parents showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, and normal recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. However, recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was reduced in the presence of 1 mM caffeine (53 +/- 8% of normal). In a colony-forming assay, UV survival of heterozygous cells was normal without caffeine but slightly reduced with caffeine. The authors suggested that XPV heterozygotes can be identified by UV sensitivity in the presence of nontoxic caffeine.

paragraphs.text: Fujiwara et al. (1981) described an 8-year-old boy (patient UV81KO) whose only symptom was acute recurrent sunburns, with no other physical or neuromental retardation. His skin had lowered minimal erythema doses at monochromatic wavelengths between 280 and 300 nm, without delayed peaking of erythema. His cultured skin fibroblasts were 5-fold more sensitive than normal cells to killing by 254-nm UV. They were also more sensitive to sunlamp UV-B, 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide, and N-hydroxy-acetylaminofluorene, but not to mitomycin C or alkylating agents. Cells from obligate heterozygotes responded normally. The authors detected no defect in nucleotide excision repair or replicative bypass. Nevertheless, the patient's cells failed to recover DNA synthesis after 254-nm UV doses of 1 and 5 J/m2, doses at which normal cells recovered. Baseline sister chromatid exchanges were raised (10 to 12 per cell vs 5 per cell in normal cells), but the rate of UV-induced exchanges was normal. After comparing these features with xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, the 11961 disorder, and Bloom syndrome, Fujiwara et al. (1981) concluded that the UV81KO disorder was distinct from all of them. They proposed it as a new photodermatosis with a defect in the recovery of DNA synthesis after UV exposure.

paragraphs.text: Masutani et al. (1999) had previously used an improved cell-free assay to isolate a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that, in XP-V cell extracts, continued replication on damaged DNA by bypassing UV-induced thymine dimers. They showed that this polymerase is a human homolog of yeast Rad30 (DNA polymerase eta), a member of a family of damage-bypass replication proteins that also includes E. coli UmuC and DinB and yeast Rev1. They found mutations in the DNA polymerase eta gene (POLH) in all XP-V cells they examined. Recombinant human DNA polymerase eta corrected the inability of XP-V cell extracts to replicate damaged DNA by bypassing thymine dimers. The authors concluded that DNA polymerase eta could be the XPV gene product.

checks.evidence_quote: Using an improved cell-free assay for trans-lesion DNA synthesis, we have recently isolated a DNA polymerase from HeLa cells that continues replication on damaged DNA by bypassing ultraviolet-induced thymine dimers in XP-V cell extracts.
checks.explanation: The paper describes this assay and isolation in the same terms.

Of the 8 mutations they identified, 7 were predicted to result in a severely truncated hRad30 protein. The authors concluded that defects in hRAD30 cause XP-V.

paragraphs.text: In a Japanese family with XPV, Itoh et al. (2000) confirmed that the patient had inherited 2 heterozygous missense mutations. Neither mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

paragraphs.text: Cleaver et al. (1980) irradiated XP variant and pigmented xerodermoid cells with UV light. They measured unscheduled DNA synthesis, strand breakage during repair, chain growth during semiconservative replication with or without caffeine, and recovery of DNA replication. The authors concluded that the common defect appeared to be loss of a gene product that allows normal cells to replicate DNA without interruption at UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. As a result, replication forks in XP variant cells were blocked more often and at lower doses. The authors suggested that this defect correlated with the high levels of actinic carcinogenesis seen in these patients.

checks.evidence_quote: XP and pigmented xerodermoid cell cultures were irradiated with ultraviolet light
checks.explanation: The abstract says 'XP' cell cultures, not specifically XP variant cultures. The comparison with the XP variant in the conclusion suggests that variant cells were included, but the abstract does not say so explicitly.

checks.explanation: All four measurements match the abstract. However, the abstract describes the cells as 'XP' cultures rather than specifically XP variant cultures.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (1991) transfected an XP variant cell line with a supF shuttle vector plasmid that had been irradiated with UV at 254 nm. Mutant frequency rose linearly with dose, with a slope 5 times steeper than previously seen in normal cells. In 52 of 53 independent mutants the change was a base substitution, and 62 of 64 substitutions involved a dipyrimidine. A.T base pairs were involved in 28% of mutations in XP variant cells, compared with 11% in normal cells, mostly at position 136. The authors suggested that XP variant cells are less likely than normal cells to incorporate dAMP opposite photoproducts, which could account for their UV hypermutability.

paragraphs.text: Using DNA combing, Despras et al. (2010) showed that in UV-irradiated XP-V cells, which lack DNA polymerase eta, the translesion synthesis defect caused a strong reduction in the number of active replication forks and a high proportion of stalled forks, in contrast to budding yeast. Extensive regions of single-strand DNA formed during replication, and the ATR/Chk1 pathway was overactivated after low UVC doses. Adding a low concentration of caffeine after irradiation lowered Chk1 activation and abolished DNA synthesis in XP-V cells. The Chk1 inhibitor UCN-01 worsened the replication defect in XP-V cells by increasing fork stalling, and like caffeine it made XP-V cells more sensitive to UVC. The authors concluded that pol eta acts at stalled forks to restart them. They further concluded that in the absence of pol eta, Chk1 becomes essential for replication to resume by alternative pathways through fork stabilization.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing xeroderma pigmentosum variant. The method measures 3 cellular DNA repair markers after UV irradiation: unscheduled DNA synthesis (UDS), recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis. Patient fibroblasts were plated on coverslips alongside normal control cells, and grain counts on nuclei were compared. Among the hereditary photosensitive disorders (XP, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome), only XP variant cells showed normal UDS and normal recovery of RNA synthesis with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (about 50% of control). Caffeine made this reduction greater. Because each of these disorders produces a different combination of the 3 markers, the method also provides a systematic basis for diagnosing them. Before this method, XP variant had been diagnosed by a postreplication repair assay together with clinical features.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (1996) described a simple autoradiographic method for diagnosing xeroderma pigmentosum variant.
checks.evidence_quote: We present here an alternative simple method for the diagnosis of xeroderma pigmentosum variant that measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography

checks.claim: The autoradiographic method of Itoh et al. (1996) measures 3 cellular DNA repair markers after UV irradiation: unscheduled DNA synthesis (UDS), recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: measures three cellular markers for DNA repair by autoradiography, unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation
checks.explanation: The abstract names the same 3 markers.

checks.claim: In the method of Itoh et al. (1996), patient fibroblasts were plated on coverslips alongside normal control cells and grain counts on nuclei were compared.
checks.evidence_quote: Fibroblasts from a patient are plated on three coverslips parallel with normal cells (control). Unscheduled DNA synthesis, recovery of RNA synthesis, and recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after ultraviolet irradiation in the patient's cells are compared with those of adjacent normal cells by counting numbers of grains on nuclei
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the same setup and comparison.

checks.claim: Among hereditary photosensitive disorders (XP, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome), only XP variant cells showed normal UDS and normal recovery of RNA synthesis with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (about 50% of control).
checks.evidence_quote: Of the hereditary photosensitive disorders including xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome, and newly established ultraviolet-sensitive syndrome, only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibit normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (approximately 50% of that of control cells).
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly, including the figure of about 50% of control.

checks.claim: Caffeine increased the reduction in recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XP variant cells.
checks.evidence_quote: This reduction of DNA synthesis is enhanced in the presence of caffeine.
checks.explanation: The abstract says caffeine enhances the reduction, which is the same as the claim.

checks.claim: Because each hereditary photosensitive disorder produces a different combination of the 3 markers, the method of Itoh et al. (1996) provides a systematic basis for diagnosing them.
checks.evidence_quote: Because each disorder yields a different combination of these three markers, this method also provides a systematic basis for the diagnosis of these diseases.

checks.claim: Before the method of Itoh et al. (1996), XP variant had been diagnosed by a postreplication repair assay together with clinical features.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum variant have been diagnosed based on a post-replication repair assay using their cells together with their clinical manifestations.

paragraphs.text: Itoh et al. (2000) noted that among the hereditary photosensitive disorders, including other XP groups, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal recovery of RNA synthesis with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation (51 +/- 6% of normal). This reduction was enhanced to 36 +/- 5% in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine. The authors also proposed that heterozygous carriers could be identified by reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis and slightly reduced UV survival in the presence of caffeine.

checks.claim: Among hereditary photosensitive disorders, including other XP groups, Cockayne syndrome, and UV-sensitive syndrome, only XPV cells showed normal unscheduled DNA synthesis and normal recovery of RNA synthesis after UV irradiation with reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: Among hereditary photosensitive disorders, including other xeroderma pigmentosum groups, Cockayne syndrome, and a newly established ultraviolet-sensitive syndrome, only xeroderma pigmentosum variant cells exhibited normal unscheduled DNA synthesis, normal recovery of RNA synthesis, but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis

checks.claim: Recovery of replicative DNA synthesis after UV irradiation in XPV cells was 51 +/- 6% of normal.
checks.evidence_quote: but reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis (51 +/- 6% the rate relative to normal controls)

checks.claim: The reduction in recovery of replicative DNA synthesis in XPV cells was enhanced to 36 +/- 5% of normal in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: This reduction of recovery of replicative DNA synthesis was enhanced in the presence of a nontoxic level of caffeine to 36 +/- 5%.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) proposed that XPV heterozygous carriers could be identified by reduced recovery of replicative DNA synthesis and slightly reduced UV survival in the presence of caffeine.
checks.evidence_quote: These results suggest that xeroderma pigmentosum variant heterozygotes can be identified by their sensitivity to ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of nontoxic levels of caffeine.
checks.explanation: The authors propose identification by UV sensitivity with caffeine; the specific markers (reduced replicative DNA synthesis recovery and slightly reduced survival) are reported findings rather than explicitly part of the proposal.

clinical_synopsis.feature: normal excision repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers

paragraphs.text: In a patient from a Japanese family with xeroderma pigmentosum variant type (XPV), Itoh et al. (2000) identified 2 heterozygous missense mutations and confirmed that both were inherited. One was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 that resulted in a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution. The other was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that affected lys589. Neither mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not name the gene POLH or explicitly state the family was Japanese.

checks.claim: Itoh et al. (2000) confirmed that both POLH mutations in the Japanese XPV patient were inherited.
checks.evidence_quote: In one family, we confirmed inheritance of two heterozygous mis-sense mutations.

checks.claim: One POLH mutation in the Japanese XPV patient was an A-to-G transition at nucleotide 1840 resulting in a lys535-to-glu (K535E) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: One mutation is an A-->G transition at nucleotide 1840 that generates a K535E mis-sense mutation.

checks.claim: The other POLH mutation in the Japanese XPV patient was an A-to-C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that affected lys589.
checks.evidence_quote: Another mutation is an A-->C transversion at nucleotide 2003 that generates a K589 mis-sense mutation.

checks.claim: Neither the POLH K535E nor the 2003A-C mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: Each of these mutations were absent in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.

(2000) found the 2003A-C mutation together with K535E in a patient from a Japanese family and confirmed that both mutations were inherited. Neither mutation was found in 52 unrelated Japanese individuals.
